$comment:
Numeric policy limits for the registry. Edit here, nowhere else — tools/ and bot/ both read this file. EVERY numeric cap in this file carries exactly one sibling saying what its relationship to an author's source tree is, and tools/validate.mjs refuses one that carries none — because the way three caps came to be enforced at ingest and mirrored nowhere was not a decision, it was an absence nobody could see. The four siblings:

`<name>_mirrors` — this number is a COPY of a constant in AstraPlugins/spec/limits.yaml, which the daemon also mirrors. It must equal it; validate.mjs compares them for real when an AstraPlugins checkout is reachable ($ASTRA_PLUGINS_DIR, else a sibling ../AstraPlugins) and prints a `note` saying the check did not run when neither exists, because a check that quietly did not happen must not look like a check that passed.

`<name>_mirrored_by` — an author CAN trip this cap from their own source tree, and a copy of the number lives in the file this names so `astra-plugin` can refuse it at pack time, BEFORE a tag exists. validate.mjs checks the copy is there and equal, and tools/check-locales.py --rules C20 checks it from the other end.

`<name>_not_author_facing` — nothing an author writes in a source tree decides this number, so there is nothing for a local check to be about. The sentence is the claim; somebody can disagree with it.

`<name>_unmirrored` — an author CAN trip it and nothing local checks it. Recorded debt, not an exemption: validate.mjs prints every one of these by name on every run. This is the state all three locale caps were in, silently, and the point of the sibling is that the next one is a visible blank instead.

ADDING A CAP: pick the sibling before the number is read anywhere. If it is `_mirrored_by`, the row in AstraPlugins has to land first and $ASTRA_PLUGINS_REF in .github/workflows/ingest.yml has to move to a commit carrying it — that pin is what build-index.yml checks the other repository out at, so a row added there reaches this comparison when the pin moves, not when it merges.

WHEN THE MIRROR CHECK GOES RED, DO NOT DELETE THE SIBLING. It greens in one keystroke by unpinning the number, and the cap goes on being enforced here either way — on an author who has already pushed a tag. That is the repair that destroys what the check was protecting — and it is now RED rather than green, because a cap with no sibling at all fails. Fix the copy, or move the pin.

WHAT THIS CANNOT REFUSE, stated so nobody believes otherwise: relabelling a true `_mirrored_by` as `_not_author_facing` with a false sentence greens everything, and no program can tell. That is the floor of any exemption list and it is the reason the sibling carries prose rather than a boolean — the escape hatch was made into a written claim somebody can read in a diff and disagree with, not closed. Measured: deleting a sibling is one keystroke and is red; writing a false one is a sentence and is green.

SCOPE: this covers the numeric caps in THIS file. Caps that live as `maxLength` in schema/version-v1.json are outside it — max_permission_reason_chars is mirrored from one, and that mirror line names a JSON pointer rather than a key. Nothing enumerates the schema's own caps in the mirrored-by direction, which is a smaller instance of exactly the gap the four siblings above close. AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY TOO, found 2026-08-23 while mirroring max_artifact_bytes: that cap's number is repeated as an artifact `size` `maximum` in BOTH schema/index-v1.json and schema/version-v1.json, and no reader compares either with this file. So this file can have copies in the schemas that nothing checks, as well as the schemas having caps here that nothing checks.
max_artifact_bytes_note:
256 MiB, the largest .astraplugin the registry will list. Deliberately below max_extract_bytes: a bundle whose COMPRESSED size approaches the daemon's UNCOMPRESSED extraction cap cannot install.

WAS `_unmirrored` UNTIL 2026-08-23, and the sentence it carried is kept here rather than deleted, because a retraction that erases its own claim leaves the next reader unable to tell a correction from a silent edit: `An author CAN trip this: astra-plugin build writes the .astraplugin and knows its size. Nothing in AstraPlugins names this number — grep for it there returns nothing — so a 300 MiB bundle builds, tags, uploads, and is refused here at the download step. It is recorded rather than fixed because fixing it is a cap on build, not a locale rule, and the review that found the locale three did not look at this one.` All of that was true. `astra-plugin build` now refuses over this cap and warns at half of it, and grep for 268435456 over there returns the row this sibling names.

THE FIRST READING OF THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG, so read it twice: `deliberately below max_extract_bytes` does NOT mean the daemon's cap already covers this one. They are different units. 500 MiB UNCOMPRESSED and 256 MiB COMPRESSED leave a window an author reaches whenever the payload is already compressed — a model, audio, video, a packed data file — and `astra-plugin`'s pack-time refusal of max_extract_bytes says nothing about it. Constructed upstream on 2026-08-23: 314,572,800 incompressible bytes packed to 314,628,268, cleared max_extract_bytes by 200 MiB, and sat 44.1 MiB over this number.

TWO OTHER COPIES OF THIS NUMBER LIVE IN THIS REPOSITORY and nothing compares them with this key: the artifact `size` `maximum` in schema/index-v1.json and the one in schema/version-v1.json. Checked, not assumed, and stated precisely because the loose version of it is wrong: the ONLY code that reads either `maximum` is tools/lib/jsonschema.mjs, the generic validator, which enforces them against a document. Nothing anywhere COMPARES either with this key. The four-sibling convention covers the numeric caps in THIS file, so a schema copy that drifted from this key would be invisible to it. Raising max_artifact_bytes is three edits.
max_versions_per_plugin_not_author_facin: Counts the version records under one plugin in THIS catalogue. A source tree has one version at a time and no history of its own listings, so there is nothing local to count.
max_artifacts_per_version_not_author_fac: Counts the artifacts attached to one GitHub release. `astra-plugin build` packs one bundle per invocation and never sees the set; the matrix that produces them lives in a workflow, and the count is a property of the release rather than of any tree.
max_keywords_not_author_facing: Keywords are curator-set. bot/lib/derive.mjs:262 says it in as many words — categories, keywords and homepage are the fields no bundle carries — and this number is currently read by nothing in this repository either, which is its own small debt and a different one.
max_keyword_length_not_author_facing: Same field, same reason: no bundle carries a keyword for a cap to apply to.
typosquat_flag_distance_not_author_facin: An edit distance between one listing's id and the ids already in this catalogue. It is not a cap on anything an author writes; its other operand is the catalogue, which no source tree can see.
max_index_bytes_not_author_facing: The size of the whole generated registry/v1/index.json, which is this repository's own artifact. No single plugin owns it and no author can measure it.
max_index_bytes_note:
1 MiB, measured on `node tools/build-index.mjs --stdout`, which is byte-for-byte what the committed registry/v1/index.json holds before signing — both come from stableStringify, so there is no pretty-printing difference between them. .github/workflows/build-index.yml compares the deploy candidate against this number; before it did, that step echoed `wc -c` and compared it to nothing, and notes/icon-readme-contract.md's `do not let the index quietly grow past a few megabytes` was enforced by nobody reading a log line.

TODAY, measured 2026-08-22 on 10 listings: 237,384 bytes. Icons are 54.6% of it, READMEs 23.6%, and all the card text together 0.36%. READ THIS BEFORE RAISING THE NUMBER: at ~23.7 KB per listing this ceiling arrives at roughly 44 listings, on ICON growth, long before locale growth reaches it. Nine locales of card text on every listing is single-digit percent; nine locales at the schema's own caps is at most 8 KiB per listing, which is what max_listing_i18n_bytes bounds, and 100 listings all at that cap is 800 KiB and would bust this too. Both cases point at the same fix, which notes/icon-readme-contract.md already sanctions: move icon_url and readme to *_url + *_sha256 pairs. Raising this number requires a written reason here.
max_listing_i18n_bytes_note:
The whole `i18n` member of ONE listing, as UTF-8 JSON. A per-listing budget on purpose: a shared ceiling would let one verbose author stop every other author's publish behind a red catalogue build whose error names no plugin. Enforced in bot/lib/locales.mjs BEFORE the block is emitted.

IT IS A BACKSTOP, NOT A SHAPE, and the measurement says so: nine locales at the schema's own caps (64 + 200 characters) in three-byte CJK is 7,399 bytes, which is the worst case a listing can legitimately reach and sits 793 bytes under this number. What it catches is text outside the basic multilingual plane, or a per-string cap that stopped being enforced. DO NOT LOWER IT toward that 7,399: a ceiling below the legitimate worst case takes a correct CJK listing's translations away and explains it with a budget. bot/tests/ingest.test.mjs asserts the headroom in that direction.
max_locale_bytes_note: One locales/<code>.json in a bundle, checked on the raw bytes BEFORE JSON.parse. inspectBundle materialises every file the manifest lists as a Buffer bounded only by max_extract_bytes (500 MB); icons are capped at 128 KiB and READMEs at 16 KiB, and locale files were capped by nothing at all. A 200 MB flat-but-valid en.json would take the ingest runner out mid-derivation and leave the submitter's issue with no verdict — the one failure mode this bot must not have. 256 KiB is about fifty times the largest locale file in any example plugin.
max_locale_keys_note: Keys in one locale file, checked after the parse and before anything walks them. The parity rules compare key sets pairwise across every locale a bundle ships, so the work is quadratic in this number and the findings it can produce are linear in it; both are bounded here rather than discovered on a runner.
